items.title: The Collapse of Rural Order in Ottoman Anatolia: Amasya 1576–1643
items.note: Village-by-village reading of tahrir and detailed avarız registers for Amasya documenting mass abandonment of rural settlements around 1600.

items.title: The 'Celâlî effect' on rural production and demography in central Anatolia
items.note: Uses serial waqf account books, which survive across the gap between tahrir and avarız registers, to trace rural output and population during the Celali years.

items.title: Problems in the Interpretations of Ottoman Rebellions in the Early Modern Period: An Analysis and Evaluation of Existing Literature on the Ottoman Celali Rebellions
items.note: Historiographical review of explanations for the Celali rebellions, from population pressure to fiscal and climatic causes.

items.title: Osmanlı Anadolusu'nda Bir İskân Hikâyesi: Bozok Sancağı'nda Aşiretler, Köylüler ve Celâlîler (16–19. Yüzyıllar)
items.note: Follows settlement in Bozok across tahrir, avarız and later registers, tracing desertion during the Celali period and later tribal resettlement.

items.title: Coping with famines in Ottoman Anatolia (1650–1850)
items.venue: An Economic History of Famine Resilience (Routledge)
items.note: Examines famine episodes and state and local responses in Anatolia after 1650, relevant to whether seventeenth-century losses were recovered.

items.title: Ottoman Text Recognition Network founded after workshop on automatic recognition of Ottoman manuscripts
items.note: Network building Transkribus models and transcription standards for handwritten Ottoman Turkish, a prerequisite for machine-reading fiscal registers at scale.

items.title: Osmanlı İmparatorluğu'nda Celali İsyanları: Chayanovyan Bakış Açısıyla Bir Değerlendirme
items.note: Reads the Celali uprisings through a Chayanovian model of the peasant household, an economic alternative to Malthusian population-pressure explanations.

items.title: Automated Transcription of Non-Latin Script Periodicals: A Case Study in the Ottoman Turkish Print Archive
items.note: Trains text-recognition models for Ottoman Turkish print, a methodological step toward machine-reading Ottoman sources.

items.title: Making of a mid-nineteenth century Ottoman gazetteer and mapping and examining late Ottoman population geography
items.who: M. E. Kabadayı, A. Sefer, G. Boykov and P. Gerrits
items.venue: Journal of the Ottoman and Turkish Studies Association 9 (2)
items.note: Explains how the projects geolocated populated places from nüfus registers, the method behind the open gazetteer used to link earlier registers to space.

items.title: Ottoman NFS Gazetteer (16,296 populated places), version 1
items.who: M. E. Kabadayı, G. Boykov, A. Sefer and P. Gerrits
items.note: Open geolocated gazetteer of Ottoman settlements that allows tahrir and avarız place names to be matched and mapped.

items.title: Tahrir ve Avârız Kayıtlarına Göre Seyyid Gazi'nin Nüfus ve İskân Yapısı
items.note: One of many recent district studies comparing fifteenth- and sixteenth-century tahrir counts with seventeenth-century avarız registers.

items.title: The Christian Population of 16th-Century Ottoman Anatolia: An Overview and Preliminary Observations on Its Location and Numbers in the 1520s
items.who: K. Moustakas, A. Kontopanagou and P. Kastrinakis
items.note: A first systematic overview of where Christians lived in Anatolia and in what numbers according to the 1520s registers, refining the sixteenth-century baseline.

items.title: Digital History, GIS, and Spatial Humanities
items.who: M. E. Kabadayı, G. Boykov and P. Gerrits
items.venue: The Cambridge Companion to Ottoman History
items.note: Surveys GIS and database approaches to Ottoman fiscal and population registers, including the gazetteers needed for comparing surveys over time.

items.title: AGRDEMAND: Markets, urban demand and agriculture in the 16th-century Eastern Mediterranean
items.note: Fellowship (2025–2027, £206,086) building a large dataset from Ottoman tax registers to map agricultural systems in the Balkans, Anatolia and the Levant during sixteenth-century demographic growth.

items.title: Plague and Migration: Rural Depopulation in the Ottoman Balkans and Anatolia during the Little Ice Age
items.note: Argues from archival letters, fiscal surveys and avarız registers that rural plague mortality and flight, not only rebellion, drove abandonment of villages.
